description: Prohibited and approval-tier operations enforced by scripts/hooks/guard.ps1 in upgrade projects (folders with .umbraco-upgrade/state.json). Matching logic lives in scripts/hooks/GuardCore.psm1; this file holds rule metadata and the data lists the logic reads.

rules.reason: Guard self-test canary blocked. The umbraco-upgrade safety hooks are active.
Force-pushing is prohibited during an Umbraco upgrade. Push without force, or ask the user to do it.
Rewriting git history (rebase, filter-branch, filter-repo, replace, update-ref -d, or amending a pushed commit) is prohibited during an Umbraco upgrade.
Deleting branches is prohibited during an Umbraco upgrade.
Discarding uncommitted changes is prohibited during an Umbraco upgrade. Stop and ask the user what to do with the changes.
Database commands are allowed only against a local database. The target is not local or cannot be verified as local.
Deploying or publishing to a remote target is prohibited during an Umbraco upgrade.
Printing environment variables wholesale or dumping secret-bearing files is prohibited. Use scripts/Read-RedactedConfig.ps1 to view configuration with secrets redacted.
Encoded PowerShell commands cannot be inspected and are blocked in upgrade projects.
state.json is changed only through scripts/state.ps1.
The content looks like it contains a secret value. Nothing in .umbraco-upgrade/ may contain secrets; redact it first.
This project is in plan-only mode. /umbraco-upgrade:plan changes nothing outside .umbraco-upgrade/.
Project files may change only after gate 3 (safety setup) has passed and the plan is approved.
Project files may change only on the recorded upgrade branch.
Database MCP tools are blocked in upgrade projects unless the user has declared a local database copy.
Pushing to a remote during an Umbraco upgrade needs your confirmation.
Starting the site runs database migrations against its configured database. Confirm the database is the declared local copy.
Running database migrations on the local copy needs your approval.
Removing a package needs your approval during an Umbraco upgrade.

This deletes tracked project files that no recorded remove-custom-feature approval names. Never remove custom functionality to make the project compile: keep the code, record an unresolved item, and ask. Retiring a feature, or deleting files a finished port replaced, is the user's decision, recorded as that approval with the paths as its scope.
Changing CI or deployment configuration needs your approval.
This writes outside the project being upgraded.
Confirm this database MCP tool targets the declared local database copy.
